content: A pinguecula is a form of conjunctival degeneration that occurs in the eye. It is a very common condition and is characterized by the presence of a yellow-white deposit on the conjunctiva, located adjacent to the limbus, which is the junction between the cornea and the sclera. Clinically, it is important to differentiate a pinguecula from a pterygium. A pterygium is a wedge-shaped area of fibrosis that appears to invade or grow into the cornea, whereas a pinguecula does not exhibit this invasive growth pattern. Pingueculae are most frequently observed in individuals living in tropical climates, and their development is strongly associated with exposure to ultraviolet (UV) radiation. Histologically, a pinguecula demonstrates degeneration of the collagen fibers within the conjunctival stroma. This is accompanied by thinning of the overlying epithelium, and in some cases, there may be evidence of calcification. Although pingueculae may slowly increase in size over time, they are benign lesions and typically do not require any form of treatment. However, if the patient is concerned about the cosmetic appearance of the lesion, surgical excision can be performed. A pinguecula is also considered one of the differential diagnoses for a limbal nodule.
